full_judgment: 8. The short fact leading to the filing of the aforesaid Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 645 of 2001 is that the respondents, Md Nazibar Rahman Talukder and others, as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 178 of 1977 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Rangpur for declaration of plaintiffs' title to the suit land measuring 25.32 and 2.73 acres as described in the schedule Ka and Kha to the plaint. The suit land originally belonged to Taher Mahmud and Hanif Mahmud. The plaintiffs are the heirs and lineal descendants of the said original owners, Taher Mahmud and Hanif Mahmud. The plaintiffs have been owning and possessing the suit land as per their respective share by amicable arrangement among themselves. The suit land was jungle land and the same was so described in CS Khatian and recorded in the name of the predecessors of the plaintiffs. Ultimately, the plaintiffs and their co-sharers cleared the jungle of the suit land in the year 1348 BS and made the same a cultivable land and since then the plaintiffs have been in possession of the same by amicable arrangement amongst themselves and with other co-sharers. The plaintiffs came to know on 3-9-1977 when the government attempted to lease out the suit land on the pretext that the government by notification under the Private Forests Act, 1945 took over the suit land for proper management and control as private forest. The plaintiffs did not know about the said notification and they were and still are in possession of the suit land. But the Karmacharies of the defendants collusively got the suit land recorded in the name of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in the SA record. After knowing about the wrong SA record in the name of the said defendants in the government, the plaintiffs in the first part of 1973 filed a Miscellaneous Case No. 26 of 1973 under section 143(A) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act which was dismissed for default on 15-6-1976 due to illness of the plaintiff No. 1 as tadbirkarak. Plaintiff No. 1 after recovery from his illness tried to file a Miscellaneous Case for setting aside the said ex parte order of dismissal but due to legal complications the plaintiffs did not file the Miscellaneous Case but instead filed the present suit for declaration of their title in respect of the suit land.
